title: 2.6.x Build fails with GCC 12.1.0 (Arch Linux)
body:
## 2.6.x Build fails with GCC 12.1.0 (Arch Linux)

Building SFML from source (2.6.x branch) fails with GCC 12.1.0.

## Environment

* Arch Linux, upgraded with `sudo pacman -Syu`
* 2.6.x branch
* GCC 12.1.0

## Steps to reproduce

1. Upgrade latest packages with `sudo pacman -Syu`
2. Install `ninja` and `cmake` if necessary
3. Build with:

```bash
git clone -b 2.6.x https://github.com/SFML/SFML.git
cd SFML
mkdir build
cmake -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/usr/bin/gcc -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/usr/bin/g++ -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -S . -B build

# Will fail, but keep going until any possible files are built
cmake --build build -j 8 -- -v -k 0 

# Run a second time to see the error in question
cmake --build build -j 8 -- -v -k 0 
```


## Expected behavior

It should build.

## Actual behavior

It did not build. :(

It fails on src/Network/SFML/Http.cpp:264 with:

```bash
/usr/bin/g++ -DSFML_NETWORK_EXPORTS -I/home/username/dev/tmp/SFML/include -I/home/username/dev/tmp/SFML/src -Wno-error -O3 -DNDEBUG -fPIC -fvisibility=hidden  -Wall -Wextra -Wshadow -Wnon-virtual-dtor -Wcast-align -Wunused -Woverloaded-virtual -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Wdouble-promotion -Wformat=2 -Wnull-dereference -Wold-style-cast -Wpedantic -Werror -Wmisleading-indentation -Wduplicated-cond -Wlogical-op -Wduplicated-branches -MD -MT src/SFML/Network/CMakeFiles/sfml-network.dir/Http.cpp.o -MF src/SFML/Network/CMakeFiles/sfml-network.dir/Http.cpp.o.d -o src/SFML/Network/CMakeFiles/sfml-network.dir/Http.cpp.o -c /home/username/dev/tmp/SFML/src/SFML/Network/Http.cpp
In file included from /usr/include/c++/12.1.0/ios:43,
                 from /usr/include/c++/12.1.0/istream:38,
                 from /home/username/dev/tmp/SFML/include/SFML/Network/IpAddress.hpp:33,
                 from /home/username/dev/tmp/SFML/include/SFML/Network/Http.hpp:32,
                 from /home/username/dev/tmp/SFML/src/SFML/Network/Http.cpp:28:
In member function ‘std::basic_streambuf<_CharT, _Traits>::char_type* std::basic_streambuf<_CharT, _Traits>::egptr() const [with _CharT = char; _Traits = std::char_traits<char>]’,
    inlined from ‘std::basic_streambuf<_CharT, _Traits>::int_type std::basic_streambuf<_CharT, _Traits>::sbumpc() [with _CharT = char; _Traits = std::char_traits<char>]’ at /usr/include/c++/12.1.0/streambuf:324:49,
    inlined from ‘std::istreambuf_iterator<_CharT, _Traits> std::istreambuf_iterator<_CharT, _Traits>::operator++(int) [with _CharT = char; _Traits = std::char_traits<char>]’ at /usr/include/c++/12.1.0/bits/streambuf_iterator.h:187:30,
    inlined from ‘void sf::Http::Response::parse(const std::string&)’ at /home/username/dev/tmp/SFML/src/SFML/Network/Http.cpp:264:37:
/usr/include/c++/12.1.0/streambuf:493:30: error: potential null pointer dereference [-Werror=null-dereference]
  493 |       egptr() const { return _M_in_end; }
      |                              ^~~~~~~~~
In member function ‘std::basic_streambuf<_CharT, _Traits>::char_type* std::basic_streambuf<_CharT, _Traits>::gptr() const [with _CharT = char; _Traits = std::char_traits<char>]’,
    inlined from ‘std::basic_streambuf<_CharT, _Traits>::int_type std::basic_streambuf<_CharT, _Traits>::sbumpc() [with _CharT = char; _Traits = std::char_traits<char>]’ at /usr/include/c++/12.1.0/streambuf:324:33,
    inlined from ‘std::istreambuf_iterator<_CharT, _Traits> std::istreambuf_iterator<_CharT, _Traits>::operator++(int) [with _CharT = char; _Traits = std::char_traits<char>]’ at /usr/include/c++/12.1.0/bits/streambuf_iterator.h:187:30,
    inlined from ‘void sf::Http::Response::parse(const std::string&)’ at /home/username/dev/tmp/SFML/src/SFML/Network/Http.cpp:264:37:
/usr/include/c++/12.1.0/streambuf:490:30: error: potential null pointer dereference [-Werror=null-dereference]
  490 |       gptr()  const { return _M_in_cur;  }
      |                              ^~~~~~~~~
cc1plus: all warnings being treated as errors
ninja: build stopped: subcommand failed.
```

The lines in question:
```cpp
            std::istreambuf_iterator<char> it(in);
            std::istreambuf_iterator<char> itEnd;
            for (std::size_t i = 0; ((i < length) && (it != itEnd)); i++)
->              m_body.push_back(*it++);
```

Looks to be dereferencing the past-the-end iterator.
